header.userPrompt:
Consolidate the Telegram receipt flow into a single bot message per receipt that is edited in place through its lifecycle, with stage text so the user sees that work is happening, and richer details on the ready/created states. Backend only (the Telegram bot), no frontend.

## Problem today (read these first)
A single receipt currently produces three separate Telegram messages, and the "Create Expense" button never goes away:
- `server/.../actions/telegram/TelegramPhotoAction.scala:57` sends a plain "Receipt saved ✓" message (its id is never kept).
- `server/.../actions/documents/ParseReceiptAction.scala:116-121` sends a second message with a "Create Expense" web-app button and DISCARDS the returned message id (`.map(_ => ())`).
- `server/.../actions/telegram/UpsertTelegramWebAppExpenseAction.scala:144-170` (`notifyTelegram`) runs when the expense is created in the mini app: because no message id was stored, `expenseMessageId` is `None`, so it sends a THIRD message with an "Edit" web-app button and stores that id; later edits edit that third message's text.
Result: the Create button message is never updated or removed, so it lingers forever, and the user gets a disconnected trail of messages.

The data model already supports one message: `server/.../repositories/models/TelegramReceipt.scala` has `chatId` and `expenseMessageId: Option[Long]`, and `TelegramReceiptRepository` has `create(id, receiptId, chatId)`, `findByReceiptId`, `findByExpenseId`, `updateExpenseMessageId(id, messageId)`. Reuse the existing `expense_message_id` column as the single bot-message id for the receipt; do NOT rename it and do NOT add an evolution.

## Telegram API helpers (`server/.../apis/TelegramApi.scala`)
Currently: `sendMessage(chatId, text): Future[Unit]`, `sendMessageWithWebAppButton(chatId, text, webAppUrl, buttonLabel): Future[Long]` (returns the message id), `editMessage(chatId, messageId, text): Future[Unit]` (EditMessageText, text only, no reply markup).

Add the two primitives the single-message flow needs, following the existing style and the bot4s models already imported:
1. A way to send the initial message and get its id back. Either a `sendMessage` variant returning `Future[Long]`, or reuse `sendMessageWithWebAppButton` where a button is wanted. Do not change the signature of the existing `Unit`-returning `sendMessage` (it has unrelated callers: `TelegramLinkAction`, `TelegramHandleTextAction`, the unlinked-user notice); add a new method instead.
2. Extend editing so it can set BOTH text and the button (so a stage edit can swap Create -> Edit -> no button). `EditMessageText` accepts `replyMarkup`; add an `editMessage` overload/variant taking an optional web-app button (label + url), or `None` for no button. Keep the existing text-only `editMessage` or fold callers into the new one, your choice, but every stage edit must be able to set the correct button.

Handle Telegram's "message is not modified" response gracefully (treat as success, do not error) and keep edits resilient: if an edit fails because the user deleted the message, fall back to sending a fresh message with the right button and store the new id (generalize the recover-and-resend pattern already in `UpsertTelegramWebAppExpenseAction`).

## Target lifecycle: one message, edited in place
Store the message id once, at photo time, then every later stage EDITS that id instead of sending a new message.

1. Received (synchronous, in `TelegramPhotoAction`): right after the telegram_receipt row exists, send an initial status message (no button) such as "Receipt received, analyzing..." using the id-returning method, and store its id via `updateExpenseMessageId`. Replace the current "Receipt saved ✓" send. This immediate ack is important: it is the only update that happens before the background jobs run. If a telegram_receipt already exists for this receipt (duplicate photo, deduped by sha256 in `uploadReceipt`), reuse/edit its existing message rather than creating another row or message; keep this minimal.
2. Classifying/reading (in `ProcessDocumentAction`): when classification completes and the document is a receipt heading into parsing, edit the stored message to a stage text such as "Reading the receipt...". When it is rejected as not a ticket (the `notATicketMessage` branch at `ProcessDocumentAction.scala:78` and `ParseReceiptAction.scala:164`), edit the stored message to that failure text with NO button, instead of sending a new message via the notifier.
3. Ready (in `ParseReceiptAction`): when parsing succeeds, EDIT the stored message to a summary plus the "Create Expense" web-app button (same `webAppUrl` as today), instead of sending a new message. Put richer detail in this summary from the parsed data available here: vendor/merchant name, total, date, and item count when available. On terminal parse failure (the existing `Left(UnsupportedKind)` / `Left(ParseError)` branches), edit the stored message to the failure text with no button. Do NOT show a failure state for a transient/retriable exception that bubbles up for job retry; only the existing terminal `Left` branches map to a failure edit.
4. Created / edited (in `UpsertTelegramWebAppExpenseAction.notifyTelegram`): edit the stored message to the saved-expense details plus the "Edit" web-app button, swapping the button from Create to Edit. Because the id is now stored from photo time, this path edits the same single message every time (including repeated edits). Keep the deleted-message fallback.

Stage texts are plain and discrete. Do NOT animate a spinner or edit on a timer (Telegram rate-limits edits to about one per second per chat, and an animation adds noise with no information). A static summary per stage is enough. Avoid em-dashes and en-dashes in all message strings (use plain punctuation; the existing middot `·` and `✓` are fine).

## Keep identical / out of scope
- Unrelated Telegram messages (`/link` replies, the text handler, the unlinked-user notice) stay as plain sends.
- No new inline callback buttons / discard action, no change to the mini app or any frontend, no dedup integration, no DB evolution, no change to how documents are parsed or classified beyond where the message is edited.
- Do not change the background-job framework, retry, or visibility-timeout behavior.

## Rules and constraints
- No silent bad data; fail loudly where the code already does; never fabricate parsed values.
- When a call passes two or more arguments of the same type (e.g. `editMessage(chatId: Long, messageId: Long, ...)` which has two `Long`s), pass them by name (a reviewer enforces this).
- Telegram send/edit failures must never break the pipeline: they are logged and recovered, exactly as the current notifier/upsert code already does.
- Follow `docs/guide/backend.md` and `docs/guide/testing.md`. Test descriptions name a single method, per `.orca/reviewers/tests.md`. Tests must not hit the real Telegram API: use a fake `TelegramApi` (mirror whatever fake/stub the existing Telegram action tests use) that records sent and edited messages.
- Match existing code style; surgical changes only; every changed line traces to this request.

## Tests
Add/extend tests for the single-message behavior using a fake `TelegramApi` that records calls:
- photo receipt sends exactly one initial message and stores its id on the telegram_receipt;
- parse-ready EDITS that same stored id and attaches the Create Expense button (no new message sent);
- not-a-ticket and terminal parse-failure EDIT the stored id to a failure text with no button (no new message);
- create via the web app EDITS the same stored id and swaps to the Edit button; a subsequent edit edits the same id again;
- unrelated sends (link/text) are unchanged.
Follow the existing Telegram action test patterns and `test-isolation` (random unique data). The full suite must pass as CI runs it.
